## We share a SilverBullet server with a team where any writer could plant malicious content. What deployment setup do the docs recommend?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Security Profiles.md] ---
### Software team

# Software team
A team, community, or any setup where a `write` member _might_ plant malicious content — deliberately or by having their own account compromised — for a more-privileged member (an admin, or a member of another space) to stumble into.

The recommended hardened profile:

* **Shell off** for spaces with untrusted writers. This removes the main capability an attacker could otherwise reach.
* **One hostname per space**, via a [[Dashboard#Bindings|custom-host binding]] rather than multiple path prefixes on one hostname. Use the primary URL for the `/.dashboard` admin surface through **Admin → Server**. Then configure a separate sub-domain per space. With this configured, the server rejects Dashboard APIs on space hosts and blocks browser requests to Dashboard APIs from other origins, including sibling subdomains.

**Why a hostname per space?** SilverBullet’s session cookie and browser origin are scoped to the hostname you’re on. A `write` member can make their space’s content run code as whoever opens it — but if each untrusted-writer space lives on its own hostname, that code runs in an origin that doesn’t hold another space’s session.

This profile benefits from wildcard DNS (or at least multiple sub-domains mapped) and a wildcard TLS certificate (or multiple custom-configured certificates).

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Install.md] ---
### Server

# Server
Run Server when you want browser access, a shared team space or a synchronization point for Desktop installations. Install it with [[Install/Docker|Docker]] or the [[Install/Server Binary|standalone binary]]. You can start on this computer and make it reachable from other devices when needed.

[[Guide/Server Setup]] covers setup and administration. [[Install/Server]] describes deployment choices and filesystem requirements.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Administration.md] ---
### Untitled

Choose the setup guide for the application you run. Desktop opens a folder on your computer. Server provides browser access and manages shared spaces. Both use the same engine underneath.

* [[Install|Choose Desktop or Server]] if you haven’t installed SilverBullet yet.
* [[Guide/Desktop Setup|Desktop setup]] covers installation, local spaces, updates and optional synchronization with a Server.
* [[Guide/Server Setup|Server setup]] covers deployment, accounts, network access, configuration and upgrades.
* [[Troubleshooting]] covers common Desktop and Server problems.
* [[Log]] explains where to find diagnostic output.
* [[Guide/Git Sync]] covers synchronizing committed revision history with a Git remote.

For writing and organizing pages, start with [[Getting Started]]. For practical workflows, see [[Guides]].

--- [vault:corpus/docs/SilverBullet.md] ---
### Find your way

# Find your way
* [[Getting Started|Start here]] — learn [[Markdown]], connect [[Page|Pages]], add [[Tag|Tags]] and [[Meta Page]] and try queries in [[Workbench]]. Each guide stands on its own.
* [[Guides]] — practical tasks and use cases for personal knowledge, team collaboration and docs as code.
* [[Administration|Setup and administration]] — install and operate Desktop or Server, and back up your space.
* [[Reference]] — look up feature behavior, syntax and APIs.
* [[Development|Contributing]] — help develop SilverBullet, its documentation and extensions.

As you will have figured, these docs run inside a read-only instance of SilverBullet. It in itself aims to be a good-practice use of [Docs as Code](https://silverbullet.md/docs-as-code). [[Guide/Reading These Docs]] explains how to inspect examples and try them in your own writable space.
